findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", giving this deploy user unrestricted control over all compute, storage, and serverless resources in the account. A leaked credential yields broad data access and the ability to launch or destroy infrastructure; permissions should be scoped to specific actions and ARNs.

A permanent IAM access key is created for a human-less service user instead of using an assumable IAM role with temporary STS credentials. The key never rotates and its secret is stored in Terraform state in plaintext when no PGP key is supplied, creating a durable credential-leak vector.

No pgp_key is configured, so the access key secret is written unencrypted into the Terraform state file; the encrypted_secret attribute referenced by the output will be empty and the real secret is only protected by whatever protects the state backend.
Exporting key material as a root module output (svc_deploy_key_material) surfaces the credential in CLI output, CI logs, and any consuming module; the output is not marked sensitive = true.

A standalone IAM user with an attached inline admin-like policy is used for deployment automation rather than a role assumed via OIDC/instance profile, and force_destroy = true allows silent removal of the user and its keys, which can mask credential tampering.
